sam: Heads up — us-west1 preemptible GPU churn spiked ~5m ago. Autoscaler started ~12 node adds, then immediate evicts, thrash. Kubelet logs show NodeTerminationHandler preemption notices (30s). Pods with local model-cache getting evicted which triggers long pulls and causes cascading scheduling delays.
ajay: Seen it too. Pods keep bouncing between the same tainted pools, backoff increases, then CA adds more nodes -> more evictions. Can we route overflow to an on-demand fallback?
maria: We do have a small warm-pool in us-west1 (size=2). Increasing helps but costs jump. Another option: a dedicated small on-demand pool with nodeAffinity for non-latency-critical jobs.
infra-bot: AUTOSCALER event: scaleUp request for gpu-preemptible-pool (12 -> 24) — unschedulable pods detected.
sam: Proposal: implement a "hotplug fallback" flow — keep a small always-on on-demand pool (label gpu-fallback=true) and update scheduler preferences to prefer preemptible nodes but allow fallback when preemptible queue length > threshold. Also tune CA to avoid immediate bounce. Pseudo-config: 
``` 
# Pod scheduling hint
nodeSelector:
  node.kubernetes.io/preemptible: "true"
# Fallback label
fallbackNodeLabel: gpu-fallback=true

# Cluster Autoscaler flags (example)
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups
--max-node-provision-time=10m
```
ajay: Also recommended: taint preemptible nodes (e.g., preemptible=true:NoExecute) and give tolerations with shorter tolerationSeconds for best-effort pods. That way we cordon sooner and avoid rescheduling churn.
lina: Can we also add a lightweight model-warm hook so pods pre-populate /tmp/model-cache in postStart? Right now evictions force full S3 pulls which are the slow part. A small init container or prefetch sidecar could shave tens of seconds.
maria: Cost tradeoff note — bumping fallback pool to 6 GPUs would reduce churn but adds ~"$X/day" (I calculated ~estimate based on on-demand rates). Alternative: increase warm-pool to 3 GPUs and enable on-demand bursting up to +4 for short windows; cheaper but slightly more complex scheduling.
sam: Next steps: 1) run a canary in us-west1 with fallback pool size=3 and preemptible taints, 2) implement scheduler preference patch (prefer preemptible but fallback), 3) apply CA flags and reduce node-provision timeout, 4) add simple model warm-up init script.
ajay: I'll own the canary tonight in low-traffic window. Will post metrics (pod restart rate, scheduling latency, CA adds) here after run. :thumbsup:
maria: I'll run cost projection for fallback vs warm-pool burst and post numbers in the morning.
sam: thanks — if canary looks stable we'll roll policy across other regions.
